review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Carry the cycle stack across sibling includes**

When a file has more than one include and a cycle goes through a later one (for example, `A` includes `C` and then `B`, while `B` includes `A`), this recursion expands only `C` because `resolveIncludes` uses the non-global `includeRegexp`. The remaining `B` node is then handled by `visitParents` through a fresh call with an empty stack; each pass replaces it with another `C` plus `B`, so build and lint never terminate. Process all sibling matches under the same stack rather than resetting the guard at the AST boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase nested assets from the inner partial**

When the outer and nested partials live in different directories and the inner file contains a relative link or image, flattening `nested.result` here discards the inner include path. The later `updatePaths` call receives only the outer `path`, while `updatePathsInIncludes` resolves targets from `dirname(includePath)` in `server/asset-path-helpers.ts`, so the generated URL points relative to the outer partial instead of the inner file. Preserve each nested file's origin or rebase its paths before flattening.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve placement validation for nested includes**

When the first include-shaped token in a partial appears inline, such as `Read (!foo.mdx!) here` or inside inline code, passing the whole unparsed file to `resolveIncludes` expands it before the AST checks can reject that context. The lint run therefore no longer emits the existing "only content on the line" error for this nested syntax, and block Markdown from `foo.mdx` can be injected into a paragraph. Parse and validate the nested node before resolving it instead of scanning arbitrary raw content.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
